shortDescription: Louis Dreyfus Company posted a rise in core first-half profits as its grains and oilseeds business drove higher volumes, the global crop merchant said on Monday.

children: Louis Dreyfus Company posted a rise in core first-half profits as its grains and oilseeds business drove higher volumes, the global crop merchant said on Monday.
LDC said that its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation reached $1.036 billion in the first six months of 2026 against $987 million in the year-earlier period.
Group net profit rose to $444 million from $418 million, although pretax profit fell to $460 million from $533 million as costs increased.
Shipped volumes rose by 2.7% year on year, helping group sales increase to $26.8 billion from $26.2 billion.
Higher prices, expansion in Central Europe, a new oilseed processing facility in Canada and volatility in energy markets supported better results for grains and oilseeds.
But wheat activity was affected by execution challenges linked to conflicts in the Middle East and Black Sea, LDC said.
have increased their full-year profit outlook, partly due to strong margins for processing crops.
Privately held LDC, controlled by Margarita Louis-Dreyfus through a family trust, does not give financial guidance.
The group's cotton and sugar divisions also recorded higher first-half operating results, while the coffee, rice and juice platforms saw profits fall.
At the end of July, it concluded the sale of a soybean crushing plant in Brazil's Parana state for $130 million.
A dividend of $229 million was paid to shareholders during the first half.
